findings.title: Thai Broadband Provider Targeted via FortiGate SSL-VPN and MeshCentral Persistence — Hunt.io original disclosure
findings.summary_md: Hunt.io published the original disclosure of an active intrusion into Thai broadband provider 3BB on September 14, 2026. The researchers discovered an open directory at 92.63.180.133:8888 containing 298 files across 30 subdirectories, including exploitation scripts for CVE-2024-21762, MeshCentral agent configuration, and device inventories showing root-level access. The attacker used MeshCentral as a persistent backdoor with the group label TH-3BB, targeting RADIUS authentication databases and maintaining anti-forensic cleanup scripts.

findings.title: Fortinet Advisory FG-IR-24-015 — CVE-2024-21762 out-of-bounds write in sslvpnd
findings.summary_md: Fortinet published advisory FG-IR-24-015 on February 8, 2024, documenting CVE-2024-21762, a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in FortiOS and FortiProxy SSL-VPN (sslvpnd) with CVSS 9.6. The advisory lists affected versions from FortiOS 6.0.x through 7.4.2 and FortiProxy 1.0.x through 7.4.2, with upgrades to 6.0.18, 6.2.16, 6.4.15, 7.0.14, 7.2.7, 7.4.3, and FortiProxy 2.0.14 or above. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on February 9, 2024, confirming in-the-wild exploitation.

findings.title: Hunting for Fortinet's CVE-2024-21762 — GreyNoise exploitation telemetry
findings.summary_md: GreyNoise published analysis on March 8, 2024, tracking active exploitation of CVE-2024-21762 following its addition to CISA's KEV catalog. The research documented proof-of-concept activity observed by GreyNoise sensors, confirming the vulnerability was being actively probed and exploited in the wild without a public exploit at the time. The post links to a full technical report on the Labs site covering the vulnerability discovery and detection development process.

findings.title: 3BB Attacker Used MeshCentral Backdoor for Root Access — The Hacker News
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported on September 14, 2026, that attackers gained full root access inside Thailand's broadband provider 3BB using MeshCentral as a stealth backdoor. The coverage cited Hunt.io's findings about the attacker targeting subscriber RADIUS databases, using CVE-2024-21762 against FortiGate SSL-VPN gateways, and deploying anti-forensic scripts that preserved MeshCentral agents while deleting other artifacts.

findings.title: Thai Broadband Provider Hacked via Fortinet Vulnerability — SecurityWeek
findings.summary_md: SecurityWeek reported on September 15, 2026, that a threat actor exploited CVE-2024-21762, a critical FortiGate SSL-VPN vulnerability, to compromise Thai broadband provider 3BB. The article noted the attacker used MeshCentral for persistence and targeted RADIUS authentication systems that store subscriber credentials, aligning with Hunt.io's disclosure of an active intrusion discovered through an exposed attacker staging server.
